LEISURE-TIME LEADERS CO-OPERATE 


TO EASE FRENCH-ENGLISH DIFFERENCES 


225 


Montreal YMCA 


After 9 p.m., Tuesday, October 10, 1967 


W. Sher 


While a period of turmoil lies ahead in the leisure time field, 
it is providing an increasing number of opportunities for warm 


co-operation between Quebec's two main language groups. 


Indicative of developing goodwill are moves underway to form 
a federation of English-speaking associations and make it a 
member of the Conféderation des Loisirs du Québec, said R. G. 


Rogers, assistant general secretary of the Montreal YMCA. 


Spokesmen for French-language groups in particular have 
wholeheartedly supported such a move, he told the Junior 


League of Montreal. 


"A much greater degree of collaboration and liaison will have 
to emerge among all the groups and organizations working in 


this field," he commented, 


While some traditional leisure time activities will disappear, 
new ones will emerge and different levels of government will 


probably become more deeply involved. 


"Leisure time, by and large, has been recuperative time, in 
between work times," he deplored. With more and more of it 
becoming available, it will become a curse instead of a 


blessing unless part of it is used to develop human capacities. 
"Recreational settings are in fact very rich educational 


settings," he insisted. "There is a whole new field here 


to be further developed and expanded." 


ai Dian
